chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan and Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who touches the basin or the ewer, then puts his hand into the vessel before pouring over his two palms. He said: “He should pour out three handfuls of the water, and if he does not do so, there is no harm. And if janabah had affected him and he put his hand into the water, there is no harm in it, so long as nothing from semen had affected his hand. But if it had affected his hand and he put his hand into the water before pouring over his two palms, then let him pour out all of the water.”

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.حَفَنَاتٍ: handfuls, referring here to three handfuls of water to be poured out
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms, which are to be washed first
key_terms.ٱلطَّسْتَ: a basin or wash-vessel touched before putting the hand into the water vessel
key_terms.ٱلْإِنَاءِ: the vessel containing the water used for purification
key_terms.ٱلْمَنِيِّ: semen, whose presence on the hand affects the ruling of the water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone puts his hand into water before washing it during purification after janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water used for purification when a person inserts his hand into the vessel before washing his palms. It distinguishes between mere contact and actual contamination by semen, ruling that the entire water must be discarded only when the hand was affected by semen before being put into the vessel.
